search_strategy: Started with a Mattermost full-text search API call for 'tinker' (one hit each in #general/#viewer), which surfaced part of the LR-schedule reversal thread. Recognizing search was too narrow, the agent then dumped every channel's full post history to /tmp/chat_<channel>.txt via the Mattermost API, and drove ~15 rounds of `grep -nE` with progressively refined keyword sets pulled from the ticket's own vocabulary (dataset_signature, CheckpointInfo, StepPlan, ResumePlan, plan_steps, step_unit, reasons, canonical_reasons, CHECKPOINT_REASONS, checkpoint-s, batches_completed, current_batch, warmup_steps, MIN_LR, ledger, trainer/TrainingStats). It also grepped the wiki for a finetune design doc (found essentially nothing) and mail (not shown as a major source in this run -- the corpus for g11 places all 47 remarks in chat). Several grep outputs were truncated by the harness's 10000-byte tool-output cap (visible '[... output limited to 10000 bytes ...]' markers), which is the most likely reason some remarks (r1.l2/l9/l11/l13/l19, r2.l1/l2/l3/l6/l11/l12/l14) were never surfaced despite being in the dumped channel files -- the agent's keyword list simply never targeted their exact wording. Despite ~12 of 47 remarks (all clues, no herrings/reversals) never being individually surfaced, every fact was still recovered because each hidden requirement was carried redundantly by 2-4 remarks and the agent found at least one clean carrier per fact. The agent cross-checked every worked numeric example against its own implementation before writing code (Analysis at line 4647, 4699), then wrote tests pinning each recorded value, ran the full local pytest suite (167 passed, including 78 new), diagnosed and cleared one pre-existing unrelated failure via git stash, pushed to a feature branch, opened/merged, and verified CI (ci.yml, 'build-test-deploy') went green and the deploy-daemon reported the release live and healthy on :9100.
end_reason: n/a -- run succeeded fully (reward 1, all 9 declared facts scored 1). Work was pushed, CI green, deployed.
notable: The ticket (line 117 of the transcript) already tells the agent the checkpoint name is 'derived deterministically from config.checkpoint_name_prefix and the step' -- but gives no template, no digit-padding, no CHECKPOINT_REASONS vocabulary, no reasons field, and no canonical_reasons semantics. All of that is entirely hidden-requirement territory that the agent reconstructed correctly from chat alone.

CI's fast gate (ci.yml, 'build-test-deploy') logged '/usr/bin/python3: No module named pytest' during its 'tests' step (transcript line 7577) -- i.e. the light gate's test step did not actually execute pytest, yet still reported success and proceeded to deploy. The agent noticed this (Analysis, line 7560: 'its tests step took under a second, so it's a light gate') and did not treat CI green alone as sufficient evidence -- it separately ran the full local pytest suite (167 passed) before calling the task done, correctly distrusting the shallow gate.

The agent encountered one failing test (tests/unittests/test_openai_online_request_processor, line 7175) after its changes, and rather than assuming it broke something, ran `git stash -u` and re-ran the same test against the pre-change tree -- confirming the failure pre-existed and was unrelated (transcript lines 7154-7175). This is a genuinely careful piece of diligence not required by the ticket.

Both r1 herrings (ledger-twin-checkpoints-dario/emil) were only ever surfaced as fragments -- the grep dumps caught the surrounding back-and-forth (reasons ordering, follow-up questions) but never the defining lines ('settled this in review - a step that trips both triggers writes both checkpoints'). The agent never adopted the herring regardless, because the reversal threads (rev1/rev2) were captured in full and unambiguously superseded it -- so the partial herring exposure caused no harm here, but a run that saw ONLY the herring fragment and missed the reversal could plausibly have gone the wrong way.

Twelve clue remarks (all clues, no herrings/reversals) were never surfaced by any grep pattern the agent used, despite the full channel text being on disk in /tmp/chat_*.txt the entire time -- the gap is entirely in keyword selection, not in access. Every one of these was redundant with at least one other remark carrying the same fact, so no fact was actually lost; this run's search strategy was thorough enough to have margin to spare.
